subsystems.name: Structural lattice
subsystems.role: the load-bearing framework that carries the shell's weight and the loads from gravity, tides and its own motion.

subsystems.name: Active support backbone
subsystems.role: holds the shell up, because no static material could survive the compressive and tidal loads by itself.

subsystems.name: Mass supply and launch
subsystems.role: delivers the trillions of tonnes of material a shell needs.

subsystems.name: Assembly and fabrication
subsystems.role: turns raw rock and metal into finished structure without a planet-sized workforce.

subsystems.name: Habitat layer
subsystems.role: the actual living surface on the inner face of the shell.

subsystems.name: Thermal and atmosphere control
subsystems.role: rejects waste heat and keeps air circulating across a surface the size of a planet.

buildSteps.title: Survey the target planet
buildSteps.detail: Map gravity, rotation, crust composition and resources, because the shell's design depends on how fast the planet spins and what it is made of.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap local industry
buildSteps.detail: Land autonomous mining and manufacturing units that build more of themselves from local rock and metal, so construction does not depend on launches from Earth.

buildSteps.title: Build the active support backbone first
buildSteps.detail: Assemble one or more orbiting rings around the planet, magnetically levitated against a stationary or slowly moving loop, to provide the force that stops the shell from collapsing inward. No material known today has the compressive strength for a static shell.

buildSteps.title: Lift material into orbit
buildSteps.detail: Use electromagnetic mass drivers, tethers or skyhooks to raise hundreds of billions of tonnes of structural material — a thin shell at roughly 1 kg per square metre around an Earth-sized planet already means on the order of 10^12 tonnes.

buildSteps.title: Weave the lattice
buildSteps.detail: Robots assemble beams and nodes section by section along the support rings, growing the framework outward until it encircles the planet.

buildSteps.title: Close in and pressurise
buildSteps.detail: Panels and a pressure membrane are fitted to the inner face, then sealed, leak-tested and slowly filled with air.

buildSteps.title: Lay the habitat surface
buildSteps.detail: Soil, water and ecosystems are placed on the inner face at roughly one standard atmosphere, with louvers or lamps creating a day/night cycle.

buildSteps.title: Commission and maintain forever
buildSteps.detail: Active support, thermal control and repair run continuously; a shell is not a finished object but a machine that must be kept stable for its whole life.

buildSteps.title: Expand or repeat
buildSteps.detail: Once the first shell is stable, extra rings and shells add more living area or enclose other bodies.

prerequisites.tech: Bulk ultra-strong materials (carbon nanotubes or graphene)
prerequisites.why: only materials near the theoretical strength limit could carry a shell's loads; today they are made in grams, not gigatonnes.
a shell needs more structure than any conceivable workforce could assemble by hand.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap in-space resource extraction and launch
prerequisites.why: asteroid mining and reusable launch are early-stage, and shell-scale mass movement is far beyond current capability.
a rigid shell is gravitationally unstable and no passive structure can hold it; support must come from moving mass.

prerequisites.tech: Planetary-scale closed-loop life support and heat rejection
prerequisites.why: space stations recycle air and water for a few people; a shell needs this for continents and must dump enormous waste heat.

pathway.milestone: orbital stations and reusable rockets make space access routine and cheap
pathway.unlocks: the logistics base to test large in-orbit structures.

pathway.milestone: in-space mining and manufacturing from asteroids or lunar material
pathway.unlocks: structural mass that never has to be lifted out of a gravity well.

pathway.milestone: working orbital rings and tethers as active-support testbeds
pathway.unlocks: proof that moving mass can hold a structure up without resting on a surface.

pathway.milestone: a partial shell — an equatorial band or ring habitat assembled around a small body
pathway.unlocks: habitat area far beyond a planet's own surface, and the techniques for scaling up.

pathway.milestone: a complete planetary shell with its own atmosphere and day/night cycle
pathway.unlocks: living area equal to an entire planet's surface, and a template for enclosing other worlds.
